mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 5% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, which raises discount rates and depresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a rise in the housing starts index (HOUST) signals weakening aggregate demand with pockets of housing resilience, which historically precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST > previous 6-month average
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not statistically distinguishable from a flat market at the 10% significance level.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 4.5% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 30% of triggered episodes, or the mean return is not significantly negative at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly contraction in the industrial production index (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average by more than 1.5% signals a broad-based supply-side slowdown, which historically precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month MA by > 1.5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not negative in at least 70% of triggered instances, or the median return is not statistically less than zero at the 1% level.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) below 2% while the federal funds rate remains above 4% for three months signals disinflation under restrictive policy, which typically coincides with positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to falling real interest rates.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < 2% AND FEDFUNDS > 4% for three months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not statistically greater than zero at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A sequential rise in real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS growth) above 0.5% per month for two consecutive months signals improving household purchasing power, which typically drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days through higher consumption and earnings expectations.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly growth > 0.5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically greater than zero at the 10% level.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate below 3.5% and a concurrent increase in average hourly earnings (not directly observed but inferred from labor market tightness via PAYEMS and UNRATE interaction) signals an overheating labor market, which historically precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to future rate hikes.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 3.5% AND PAYEMS growth > 0.4% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 35% of triggered episodes, or the mean return is not significantly negative at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in real retail sales (proxied by RSAFS) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals weakening consumer demand, which typically precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to lower corporate revenue expectations.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < 12-month MA for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 45% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically less than zero at the 10% level.
